lead.text: For a typical person (a 37-year-old married man born in the United States, a high-school graduate in a private-sector professional job, working 40 hours a week with no capital gains or losses), the model predicts a chance of a low income ($50,000 or less) of about {{C001.risk.from|pct}}.
The model adds up ten parts: one large weighted sum of most of the inputs, plus nine more, each built around one or two inputs.

sentences.text: Through this weighted sum, for a typical person, being married to a member of the armed forces rather than to a civilian spouse lowers the predicted chance of a low income ($50,000 or less) from about {{C073.risk.from|pct}} to {{C073.risk.to|pct}}, and a higher age lowers it steadily, from about {{C074.risk.from|pct}} at {{C074.statement.change.from}} to about {{C074.risk.to|pct}} at {{C074.statement.change.to}}.

Capital gains lower it steadily, from about {{C076.risk.from|pct}} at {{C076.statement.change.from}} to about {{C076.risk.to|pct}} at {{C076.statement.change.to}}, flattening out near the bottom because the predicted chance cannot go much lower.

A higher education level lowers it in an uneven way, from about {{C077.risk.from|pct}} at {{C077.statement.change.from}} to about {{C077.risk.to|pct}} at {{C077.statement.change.to}} (for a typical person with the highest education such people have in the data: 11th grade, then a bachelor's degree).
A typical woman rather than a typical man (so, as such women are in the data, never married and not living in a family) has it raised from about {{C082.risk.from|pct}} to about {{C082.risk.to|pct}}.

Together with the weighted sum, capital gains lower the predicted chance of a low income ($50,000 or less) slowly at first, then faster: for a typical person, from about {{C002.risk.from|pct}} at {{C002.statement.change.from}} to about {{C002.risk.to|pct}} at {{C002.statement.change.to}}, flattening out near the bottom because the predicted chance cannot go much lower.

This part adds the extra fall for large gains: through it alone, it makes no change until about {{C130.shape.points_text.at}}, then the chance falls steadily, from about {{C130.risk.from|pct}} at {{C130.statement.change.from}} to about {{C130.risk.to|pct}} at {{C130.statement.change.to}}.
The fall is a little smaller for a typical person born in Jamaica: from about {{C139.risk.groups[0].from|pct}} to about {{C139.risk.groups[0].to|pct}}, slowly at first, then faster.

This part acts on {{C162.statement.n_active}} of the {{C162.statement.n}} training people, and through it age adds to the predicted chance of a low income ($50,000 or less) once it rises above about {{C161.statement.threshold.text}}; for {{C161.statement.support_check.exceptions}} of the {{C161.statement.support_check.n}} training people it already acts below that.

Through this part, for a typical person, going from {{C158.statement.change.from}} to {{C158.statement.change.to}} raises the chance from about {{C158.risk.from|pct}} to about {{C158.risk.to|pct}}, with no change until about {{C158.shape.point.text}}, then steadily, flattening out near the top because the predicted chance cannot go much higher.

With the weighted sum, the whole model's chance is lowest at about {{C018.shape.points_text.turning}} and higher either side: for a typical person it goes from about {{C018.risk.from|pct}} at {{C018.statement.change.from}} to about {{C018.risk.to|pct}} at {{C018.statement.change.to}}.

Working more hours lowers the predicted chance of a low income ($50,000 or less) steadily up to about {{C164.shape.point.text}}, then no further: for a typical person, from about {{C164.risk.from|pct}} at {{C164.statement.change.from}} to about {{C164.risk.to|pct}} at {{C164.statement.change.to}}.

Longer hours act only while they stay below about {{C165.statement.threshold.text}} (checked for all {{C165.statement.support_check.n}} training people, with {{C165.statement.support_check.exceptions}} exceptions).

This part acts on the {{C169.statement.n_active}} training people who are self-employed and not incorporated, and for a typical such person it raises the predicted chance of a low income ($50,000 or less) from about {{C169.risk.from|pct}} without it to about {{C169.risk.to|pct}} with it.

Living with other relatives rather than in another household role raises the predicted chance of a low income ($50,000 or less) for a typical person from about {{C171.risk.from|pct}} to about {{C171.risk.to|pct}}.

A preschool education rather than any other raises the predicted chance of a low income ($50,000 or less) for a typical person with that education (and the education level of 1 such people have in the data) from about {{C173.risk.from|pct}} to about {{C173.risk.to|pct}}.

Being born in Trinidad and Tobago rather than elsewhere raises the predicted chance of a low income ($50,000 or less) for a typical person from about {{C176.risk.from|pct}} to about {{C176.risk.to|pct}}; the part acts on the {{C179.statement.n_active}} training people born there.

Being born in Yugoslavia rather than elsewhere lowers the predicted chance of a low income ($50,000 or less) for a typical person from about {{C181.risk.from|pct}} to about {{C181.risk.to|pct}}, while working for a state government moves it from about {{C182.risk.from|pct}} to about {{C182.risk.to|pct}}.
This part barely changes the predictions: the largest change when it is switched off is {{C186.statement.max_change_in_risk|pct}}.

ann_122.proposed: A capital-gains step that lowers the predicted chance of a low income ($50,000 or less) once gains pass about {{C143.shape.points_text.at}} (for a typical person, through it, from about {{C143.risk.from|pct}} to about {{C143.risk.to|pct}} at {{C143.statement.change.to}}); with the rest of the model the fall is smaller for a typical person born in Ecuador.

ann_123.proposed: A second capital-gains step that acts on {{C156.statement.n_active}} of the {{C156.statement.n}} training people and lowers the predicted chance of a low income ($50,000 or less) once gains pass about {{C148.shape.points_text.at}}; with the rest of the model the fall is smaller for a typical person born in Jamaica.

ann_124.proposed: An age step that raises the predicted chance of a low income ($50,000 or less) once age rises above about {{C161.statement.threshold.text}} (for a typical person, through it, from about {{C158.risk.from|pct}} at {{C158.statement.change.from}} to about {{C158.risk.to|pct}} at {{C158.statement.change.to}}), so that in the whole model the chance is lowest at about {{C018.shape.points_text.turning}} and higher either side.

ann_126.proposed: Working fewer hours raises the predicted chance of a low income ($50,000 or less), with hours mattering up to about {{C164.shape.point.text}} and no further: for a typical person, from about {{C164.risk.to|pct}} at {{C164.statement.change.to}} to about {{C164.risk.from|pct}} at {{C164.statement.change.from}}.

ann_125.proposed: Being self-employed and not incorporated raises the predicted chance of a low income ($50,000 or less): for a typical such person, from about {{C169.risk.from|pct}} without this part to about {{C169.risk.to|pct}} with it.

ann_119.proposed: Living with other relatives raises the predicted chance of a low income ($50,000 or less) for a typical person from about {{C171.risk.from|pct}} to about {{C171.risk.to|pct}}.

ann_121.proposed: A preschool education raises the predicted chance of a low income ($50,000 or less) for a typical person with that education from about {{C173.risk.from|pct}} to about {{C173.risk.to|pct}}; the part acts on the {{C174.statement.n_active}} preschool-educated training people.

ann_118.proposed: Being born in Trinidad and Tobago raises the predicted chance of a low income ($50,000 or less) for a typical person from about {{C176.risk.from|pct}} to about {{C176.risk.to|pct}}; the part acts on the {{C179.statement.n_active}} training people born there.

ann_117.proposed: Being born in Yugoslavia lowers the predicted chance of a low income ($50,000 or less) for a typical person from about {{C181.risk.from|pct}} to about {{C181.risk.to|pct}}; working for a state government barely moves it.

ann_120.proposed: This part barely changes the predictions: the largest change when it is switched off is {{C186.statement.max_change_in_risk|pct}}.
